info.title: Instant API
info.description: Manage Instant Cloud apps, deployments, databases, domains and buckets.

bearer.description: An access token from `instant login` or an API token (inst_…).

get.description: The signed-in person, the organization this connection acts in, and whether it can make changes (access `write`) or only read (`read`). Call it first to know where you are.
Organizations this connection can act in, with your role in each. An MCP connection and an API token work in one organization; the CLI can switch between all of yours.
Regions apps, databases and buckets can run in. Pass a region's `code` when creating one; leave it out for the default region.
The organization's plan, credit balance and billing state. Check it before creating large resources: creating anything fails while the organization is out of credits or over its plan's limits.
Apps in the organization with their URL, status, source (a GitHub repository or an upload) and latest deployment.

post.description: Creates an app. With source `github` (the default) it builds `repository` on every push to `branch`, and the first deploy starts at once. With source `upload` there is no repository: deploy code from your computer by running `instant deploy` in the project's directory (the Instant CLI). Every app gets an HTTPS URL on its own subdomain. Build and start commands are detected from the code when left out.

name.description: Shown in the dashboard; the subdomain is made from it

repository.description: owner/repo on GitHub, required for source github

branch.description: Branch to deploy; defaults to the repository's default branch

rootDirectory.description: Directory of the app inside the repository, for monorepos

memoryMb.description: Memory for each instance in MB: 512, 1024…

replicas.description: How many instances serve the app

size.description: Leave out for the smallest size, 0.25 vCPU and 512 MB

deploy.description: Start the first deploy now (GitHub apps only)

get.description: One app: URL, domains, size, build settings, source and its latest deployment.

schema.description: The app's slug (as shown by list_apps) or its id

patch.description: Renames an app or changes how it is built: branch, root directory, build and start commands, and whether pushes deploy automatically. Pass null to go back to the detected command. Changes apply on the next deploy.

schema.description: The app's slug (as shown by list_apps) or its id

post.description: Changes the vCPUs and memory of each instance and the number of instances. A new instance count applies at once; a new CPU or memory size applies on the next deploy (`requiresRedeploy`). Bigger sizes cost more per hour.

schema.description: The app's slug (as shown by list_apps) or its id

post.description: Stops the app so it no longer serves requests or costs anything. Its settings, domains and deployments are kept; resume it any time.

schema.description: The app's slug (as shown by list_apps) or its id

post.description: Starts a paused app again with its last deployment.

schema.description: The app's slug (as shown by list_apps) or its id

get.description: GitHub repositories Instant can build, from the accounts where you installed the Instant GitHub app. Use one as `repository` in create_app.

post.description: Starts a deployment and returns at once; follow it with get_deployment or get_build_logs. A GitHub app builds the head of its branch, or `commit` when given. An app without a repository rebuilds its last upload. To deploy local files, run `instant deploy` in the project's directory instead (the Instant CLI uploads them).

commit.description: Git commit to deploy; defaults to the branch head

uploadId.description: Set by the CLI after uploading the code

message.description: Shown instead of a commit message for an upload

git.description: Git state of the uploaded code, sent by the CLI

get.description: An app's deployments, newest first, with status, commit or upload, and why a failed one failed.

post.description: Returns a URL to PUT a gzipped tarball of the project's source to (at most 100 MB). Then call deploy_app with the upload's id. The CLI does both for you.

get.description: One deployment's status and timing. Status moves queued → building → deploying → active; failed carries a reason and message. Poll it every 10–20 seconds while a deploy runs.
The deployment's log: build output, then the app's output while it started. The last `limit` lines come back; a failed build's error is usually near the end.

get.summary: Get fix suggestions for a failed build
get.description: For a failed deployment, what Instant recognised in the log (a missing variable, a wrong start command, a lockfile problem…) and how to fix it. Empty when nothing known matched; then read get_build_logs.

post.description: Stops a deployment that is still queued, building or deploying. The app keeps serving its current version.
Deploys an earlier deployment's code again (its commit or its upload). Find one with list_deployments.

deployment.description: The earlier deployment to go back to

get.description: What the running app printed, newest last, across all its instances. Pass `before` (the `cursor` of the oldest line you have) to read further back. Use it to debug errors after a deploy went live.

schema.description: Cursor of the oldest line already read

get.description: CPU (cores), memory (MB), network (bytes per second) and restarts for an app over a window, with its limits. A peak near the memory limit or restarts above zero explain crashes; raise the size with scale_app.
An app's environment variables. Secret values are hidden unless `reveal` is true, which needs full access and is recorded in the audit log.

put.description: Creates or updates an app's environment variables in one call. Keys are UPPER_CASE. List a key in `secret` to hide its value in the dashboard. Variables apply on the next deploy: call deploy_app to use them now.

delete.description: Removes one environment variable from an app. Variables apply on the next deploy: call deploy_app to use them now.

get.description: The app's own subdomain and its custom domains, each with whether DNS is verified and the certificate's state.

post.description: Adds a custom domain to an app and returns the DNS records to create at the domain's DNS provider. Instant checks the records every minute and issues the HTTPS certificate once they resolve; check_domain checks now.
Checks a custom domain's DNS records now and returns whether it is verified, the certificate's state, and the records still needed.

get.description: PostgreSQL, MySQL and Redis databases in the organization with their status and size.

post.description: Creates a PostgreSQL, MySQL or Redis database on Instant's private network. It starts as `creating` and is usually `running` within a minute; check with get_database. Pass `connect` to put its connection string into apps' variables (DATABASE_URL, or REDIS_URL for Redis) and redeploy them when it is ready.

version.description: Defaults to the engine's current version (PostgreSQL 16, MySQL 8.4, Redis 7.4)

size.description: Leave out for the smallest size

connect.description: Slugs or ids of apps to connect

get.description: One database's status, engine, size and hosts. Connection strings come from get_database_credentials.

patch.description: Changes a database's vCPUs, memory or disk. The database restarts with the new size, which takes it offline for a few seconds. Disk can only grow.

post.description: Stops a database: apps using it lose their connection until it is started again. Its data is kept.

get.description: The private connection string apps on Instant use (DATABASE_URL), the public one for tools on your computer (DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL), and the user and password. Needs full access; recorded in the audit log. Prefer connect_database to give an app its URL.

post.summary: Connect a database to an app
post.description: Writes the database's private connection string into an app's variables (DATABASE_URL by default, REDIS_URL for Redis) and redeploys the app unless `redeploy` is false.

Runs one SELECT, SHOW, EXPLAIN or WITH … SELECT on a PostgreSQL or MySQL database and returns up to 200 rows. It runs in a read-only transaction, so it cannot change data or the schema: make changes through the app's migrations.

get.description: CPU, memory and disk use of a database over a window, with its size limits.
Backups of a database, newest first, with their size and state. Restoring one is done in the dashboard.

post.description: Starts a backup of a database. Take one before a risky migration.

get.description: S3-compatible object storage buckets in the organization, with their size and object count.

post.description: Creates an S3-compatible bucket. Private by default (objects need a key); `public` makes objects readable by anyone with the link. Names are global: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

connect.description: Slugs or ids of apps that get S3_* variables for this bucket

post.summary: Connect a bucket to an app
post.description: Gives an app its own access key to a bucket and writes S3_ENDPOINT, S3_REGION, S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY into its variables, then redeploys it unless `redeploy` is false.

prefix.description: Variable name prefix, e.g. S3_ or UPLOADS_

get.description: Every line of the deployment's log as it is written, then an `event: done` with the final status.

200.description: Server-sent events: `data:` lines carry one log line as JSON; `: ping` comments keep the connection open.

get.description: Recent output of the running app, then new lines as they come. Runs until the client disconnects.

200.description: Server-sent events: `data:` lines carry one log line as JSON; `: ping` comments keep the connection open.
